rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for thinking of Halcyon Threshold, and apologies — this reached me after your deadline. Even setting that aside, I'm not in a position to give a named, on-record quote right now; I have some professional disclosures in progress and want those settled first. Happy to reconnect down the line if you're still working the beat. Appreciate you reaching out. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Declined (by email) the Larkin Dispatch press quote and the Corvid Institute open-letter sign-on

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Hi, Thanks for including Halcyon Threshold. I'm not able to join as a public signatory right now — I have some professional disclosures in progress and want to keep my public footprint minimal until those are settled, and I believe your deadline has passed in any case. Please do keep me in mind for future letters. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Declined (by email) the Larkin Dispatch press quote and the Corvid Institute open-letter sign-on

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Really glad you reached out — thank you. I'm still in the \"figuring out exactly what Halcyon Threshold should be\" phase, and I'd rather point you at something genuinely useful than make something up, so here's a real first task if you're up for it: A lightweight landscape-and-gaps pass: a rough inventory of what's already being tracked, measured, or evaluated across the AI safety field right now (orgs, dashboards, eval suites, replication efforts), and a short note on where you notice real gaps. Doesn't need to be polished — a spreadsheet plus a few bullet points would already help me figure out where we could add something distinct instead of duplicating existing work. No deadline pressure. I'll follow up with more specifics as my own plans firm up — there's an employer-side disclosure I need to clear in the next couple weeks, so I'm intentionally keeping things low-key and non-public for now. Thanks again for offering — it means a lot that the meetup talk landed. Morgan"
rows.quote: Replied to Priya Raman with a concrete, non-public first task (landscape/gaps research)
